newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Stadshypotek wants more bid information.
newsitem.headline: Stadshypotek wants more bid information.

text.p: The board of Swedish mortgage bank Stadshypotek on Friday said it does not have enough information to form an opinion about a takeover bid by Swedish bank Handelsbanken.
"We need some additional information before we do an evaluation," Stsadshypotek chairman Gosta Renell told Reuters.
Renell could not say when the board would have enough information to form an opinion but he did not expect it to happen on Friday.
Renell said the managements of Stadshypotek and Handelsbanken had met and talks were continuing.
Handelsbanken, Swedish largest bank by assets, launched a 22.9 billion crown ($3.4 billion) bid on the mortgage bank on Thursday.
The bid was given initial conditional approval by the state, which is the largest single owner of Stadshypotek and is currently selling its 34 percent stake by auction.
Finance Minister Erik Asbrink said he approved the bid unless a higher offer was made.

On November 25 Stadshypotek and Swedish insurer Skandia proposed a merger which valued the bank at around 21 billion crowns. The proposal was strongly opposed by the government and Finance Minister Erik Asbrink.
Skandia on Friday said it was continuing with its prospectus for Stadshypotek and would release more information next week.
-- Peter Fellman, Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1006 ($ = 6.802 Swedish Crowns)
